## Scope

Initialize the auth-service module as a Spring Boot backend service.

## Context

This is the first test ticket for running the full DevFlow cycle:

Jira → DevFlow → GitLab branch → AI planning → code generation → validation → PR

## Repository

## Requirements

- Create a new Spring Boot project for auth-service.
- Use Maven project metadata:
  - groupId: com.az.auth
  - artifactId: auth-service
  - version: 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT
  - name: auth-service
  - basePackage: com.az.auth
  - Java Version: 21
- Support runtime environments:
  - local
  - dev
  - staging
  - prod
- The project should be buildable and testable locally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The repository contains a valid Spring Boot project.
- Maven build succeeds.
- Basic application startup test exists.
- Environment profile configuration exists for local, dev, staging, and prod.
- DevFlow can create a GitLab branch and pull request for this ticket.
features.name: Initialize Auth Service Project

features.description:
## Scope

Add Docker support for local development of the auth-service module.

## Context

This is the second ticket to continue testing the full DevFlow cycle for the Spring Boot auth-service module.

The auth-service module is a Maven project defined by pom.xml.

## Repository

## Requirements

- Add a Dockerfile at the repository root.
- The Dockerfile must build and start the auth-service module.
- The Dockerfile must use eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine as the base image.
- The built image must contain the generated auth-service JAR file.
- Add .dockerignore if useful for local Docker build performance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- docker build -t auth-service:local . succeeds.
- The built Docker image contains the auth-service JAR file.
- docker run --rm auth-service:local starts the container successfully.
- All generated paths are relative to the repository root.
- No generated file violates allowed paths, allowed extensions, or forbidden path rules.
features.name: Local development environment with Docker

features.description:
## Scope

Establish the CI pipeline foundation for the auth-service repository to support development environment delivery readiness.

This task is limited to repository-owned CI build and validation capabilities.

### Allowed Artifacts

- .github/workflows/*
- Dockerfile
- .dockerignore
- pom.xml
- src/main/resources/application-dev.yml
- src/main/resources/application.yml
- src/main/resources/application-*.yml

## Context

The repository currently lacks a development CI pipeline capable of:

- Building the Spring Boot application
- Running automated tests
- Executing code quality validation
- Building Docker images
- Providing a reusable CI foundation for future deployment stages

A previous execution identified that GitHub Actions workflow files are required to satisfy the requested capability.

Scope Compatibility Analysis detected:

Missing inferred artifacts:
- .github/workflows/*

The repository contract must explicitly allow GitHub Actions workflow files before implementation can proceed.

Infrastructure deployment artifacts were also inferred but are not required for this foundation task and should remain outside the scope of AUTH-233.

## Repository

Repository: auth-service

Technology Stack:

- Java
- Spring Boot
- Maven
- Docker
- GitHub Actions

## Requirements

### R1. GitHub Actions Workflow Foundation

Create a GitHub Actions workflow under:

.github/workflows/

The workflow must:

- Trigger on pull requests
- Trigger on pushes to the development branch
- Execute repository validation steps

### R2. Maven Build Validation

The workflow must:

- Restore dependencies
- Build the application
- Execute Maven tests
- Fail the workflow when build or test execution fails

### R3. Code Quality Validation

Integrate repository code-quality validation.

The workflow must support:

- SonarQube or SonarCloud execution
- Secure token-based configuration
- Quality gate enforcement when configured

### R4. Docker Image Build Validation

The workflow must:

- Build the repository Docker image
- Validate Docker build success
- Fail when Docker build fails

### R5. Development Pipeline Structure

The workflow must provide a reusable CI foundation that can later be extended for:

- staging deployment
- production deployment
- image publication
- GitOps deployment

without redesigning the workflow architecture.

### R6. Profile Support

Development profile configuration must remain compatible with pipeline execution.

If required, development profile configuration may be added or updated under:

src/main/resources/application-dev.yml

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1

A GitHub Actions workflow exists under:

.github/workflows/

### AC2

Pipeline execution performs:

- Maven build
- Maven test execution

successfully.

### AC3

Pipeline includes code-quality validation support.

### AC4

Pipeline builds the repository Docker image successfully.

### AC5

Workflow fails when:

- build fails
- tests fail
- Docker build fails

### AC6

Pipeline executes automatically for supported repository events.

### AC7

Implementation remains limited to repository-owned CI artifacts.

### AC8

No deployment infrastructure artifacts are created.

## Out of Scope

The following artifacts are intentionally excluded from AUTH-233:

applications/*
argocd/*
deployment.yaml
helm/*
k8s/*

The following capabilities are also excluded:

- Kubernetes deployment
- ArgoCD deployment
- GitOps application manifests
- Helm charts
- Production deployment automation
- Staging deployment automation
- Container registry publishing

These should be implemented in a separate infrastructure-scoped task.

## Business Rules

### BR1

AUTH-233 establishes CI foundation only.

### BR2

Deployment infrastructure ownership remains outside this repository.

### BR3

The task must not introduce Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD, or GitOps deployment artifacts.

### BR4

The workflow must be reusable for future environments without requiring a complete redesign.

## Technical Notes

The GitHub Actions workflow must be implemented as a single owned artifact.

Do not split .github/workflows/ci.yml into multiple subtasks by workflow stage.

Only one Work Package may own:

.github/workflows/ci.yml

Build, test, quality, and Docker build steps must be implemented together inside that same workflow-file Work Package.

Separate Work Packages are allowed only when they own different files, such as:

- Dockerfile
- .dockerignore
- pom.xml
- src/main/resources/application-dev.yml
features.name: Dev Environment Delivery Pipeline Foundation

features.description:
## Background

AUTH-233 established the initial auth-service project and has been completed and merged into the dev branch.

The repository currently supports local Maven and Docker-based development but does not yet provide a production-ready GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline.

The previous GitLab implementation supported:

- Maven build
- Automated testing
- Docker image build
- Container registry publishing
- Production deployment
- Flyway migration execution

An equivalent GitHub-native solution is required.

## Problem

The auth-service repository currently lacks:

- GitHub Actions build automation
- Automated test execution
- GitHub Container Registry publishing
- Production deployment automation
- Production migration workflow

This prevents repeatable and auditable release management using GitHub.

## Goal

Implement a production-ready GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline for auth-service.

The solution should support:

- Build validation
- Automated testing
- Docker image publication
- Production deployment workflow
- Production Flyway migration workflow

while remaining compatible with the existing auth-service repository structure.

## Scope

The implementation may include:

- GitHub Actions workflow definitions
- Build stage implementation
- Test stage implementation
- Docker image build workflow
- GitHub Container Registry integration
- Production deployment workflow
- Production migration workflow
- CI/CD documentation updates
- Required GitHub Actions configuration

Planning and implementation must use the current state of the dev branch as the source of truth.

Existing repository files may be used as planning context.

## Planning Constraints

The whole .github/workflows/deploy.yml file must be owned by one Work Package only.

Do not split .github/workflows/deploy.yml into separate Docker publish, deployment, and migration Work Packages.

Docker image build, GHCR push, production deployment, and Flyway migration should be grouped into the same deploy workflow Work Package if they are implemented in .github/workflows/deploy.yml.

Subtask validation commands must not require GitHub Actions runtime, Docker daemon, production credentials, or the act CLI unless explicitly available in the repository environment.

DevFlow must decompose this ticket by durable owned artifact, not by CI/CD stage.

GitHub Actions build, test, Docker build, Docker push, production deployment, and production migration may be implemented inside workflow YAML files.

Do not create separate Work Packages for build stage, test stage, Docker stage, push stage, deploy stage, or migration stage if they modify the same workflow file.

No two Work Packages may own the same workflow file.

Expected ownership boundaries should be grouped around durable artifacts, for example:

- .github/workflows/ci.yml
- .github/workflows/deploy.yml
- README.md

A Work Package must own at least one target file, except for a final integration validation Work Package.

Avoid empty ownedTargetFiles unless validationScope is integration.

## Out of Scope

- Business feature development
- API functionality changes
- Authentication logic changes
- Database schema changes unrelated to deployment
- Blue/Green deployment
- Canary deployment
- Multi-service orchestration
- Infrastructure provisioning outside auth-service deployment requirements

## Acceptance Criteria

- GitHub Actions validates repository build successfully.
- GitHub Actions executes automated tests.
- Docker images can be built through GitHub Actions.
- Docker images can be published to GitHub Container Registry.
- A production deployment workflow exists.
- A production migration workflow exists.
- Required GitHub Secrets are documented.
- No secrets are committed into source control.
- The solution remains compatible with the current auth-service repository.
- The implementation is executable through the repository's GitHub Actions environment.

## Validation

Evidence should demonstrate:

- Successful Maven build execution
- Successful automated test execution
- Successful Docker image build
- Successful image publication to GitHub Container Registry
- Successful production deployment workflow execution
- Successful production migration workflow execution

The validation approach should be determined during planning and implementation.
features.name: GitHub Actions Production CI/CD Pipeline

features.description:
## Goal

Enable the auth-service testing environment to connect to a PostgreSQL database using Spring Boot, Hibernate, and JPA.

The implementation should provide the required dependencies, application configuration, and testing configuration necessary to establish database connectivity during testing and validation phases.

The outcome should allow DevFlow integration validation and future persistence-related features to execute against a PostgreSQL database.

## Scope

### Dependency Configuration

Add and configure the required PostgreSQL, Hibernate, and Spring Data JPA dependencies.

### Spring Database Configuration

Add Spring datasource configuration required for PostgreSQL connectivity during testing.

### Hibernate Configuration

Add Hibernate/JPA configuration required for database access and entity management.

### Testing Configuration

Provide testing-phase database configuration that allows Spring Boot tests to initialize successfully with PostgreSQL.

### Validation

Verify that the application context starts successfully and database connectivity can be established during testing.

## Out of Scope

The following items are explicitly excluded:

- Production database provisioning
- Kubernetes deployment changes
- Flyway migrations
- Liquibase migrations
- Entity implementation beyond what is required for connectivity validation
- Business domain model implementation
- Repository layer implementation unrelated to connectivity validation
- CI/CD pipeline changes
- Monitoring and observability changes
- Performance tuning
- Security hardening of database credentials

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1 — PostgreSQL Dependencies

Required PostgreSQL-related dependencies are added and resolved successfully.

### AC2 — Hibernate/JPA Dependencies

Required Hibernate and Spring Data JPA dependencies are configured successfully.

### AC3 — Spring Datasource Configuration

Spring datasource configuration exists and supports PostgreSQL connectivity during testing.

### AC4 — Hibernate Configuration

Hibernate/JPA configuration is present and compatible with PostgreSQL.

### AC5 — Application Startup

Spring Boot application starts successfully with the configured database settings.

### AC6 — Test Context Initialization

Spring testing context initializes successfully using the configured PostgreSQL datasource.

### AC7 — Validation Evidence

Validation evidence demonstrates successful application startup and database connectivity initialization.

## Validation Requirements

The implementation should provide executable validation demonstrating:

- Dependency resolution succeeds
- Spring application context starts successfully
- Hibernate initialization succeeds
- PostgreSQL datasource initialization succeeds
- Test context initialization succeeds

## Deliverables

Expected deliverables may include:

- Dependency configuration updates
- Spring datasource configuration
- Hibernate/JPA configuration
- Testing configuration updates
- Validation evidence

Exact file ownership and implementation decomposition will be determined by DevFlow planning.

## Risks

### Configuration Compatibility

Dependency version compatibility issues may prevent application startup.

### Environment Configuration

Incorrect datasource configuration may prevent database connectivity.

### Validation Environment

Testing environment availability may affect validation execution.

## Definition of Done

The ticket is complete when:

- PostgreSQL connectivity configuration is implemented.
- Hibernate/JPA configuration is implemented.
- Spring Boot starts successfully with the configured database settings.
- Testing context initializes successfully.
- Validation evidence is produced.
- All generated Work Packages are completed and reconciled.
features.name: Add PostgreSQL Database Connectivity for Testing Phase

## Scope

Add Kubernetes manifests for deploying auth-service to a Kubernetes cluster.

The deployment should run the existing auth-service Docker image and expose the application through a Kubernetes Service.

Container images should be pulled from GitHub Container Registry (GHCR).

## Context

AUTH-233, AUTH-238, AUTH-247, and AUTH-250 have already been completed and merged to the dev branch.

The auth-service application can already be built and packaged as a Docker image.

This ticket introduces the initial Kubernetes deployment manifests required to run the service inside a Kubernetes environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Deployment Manifest

- A Kubernetes Deployment manifest exists for auth-service.
- The Deployment references a Docker image hosted in GitHub Container Registry.
- The Deployment defines the application container and required runtime configuration.
- The Deployment is suitable for a non-production environment.

### Service Manifest

- A Kubernetes Service manifest exists for auth-service.
- The Service exposes the application within the cluster.
- The Service routes traffic to the auth-service pods.

### Validation

- Kubernetes manifests are syntactically valid.
- The manifests can be applied to a Kubernetes cluster.
- The Deployment and Service reference the same application workload.

## Out of Scope

- Ingress configuration
- Helm charts
- Horizontal Pod Autoscaling
- Secrets management
- ConfigMaps
- CI/CD pipeline changes
- Production hardening
- Monitoring and observability

features.description:
### Goal

Publish the auth-service Docker image to GitHub Container Registry as part of the CI workflow.

### Context

The current CI workflow builds the Maven artifact and builds a Docker image, but the image is not pushed to GHCR. Kubernetes deployment requires a published image that can be pulled by the cluster.

### Scope

Update the GitHub Actions CI workflow for auth-service Docker image publishing.

### Requirements

The CI workflow must build and publish the auth-service Docker image to GHCR.

The workflow must support branch-based image tagging for development and release use cases.

The workflow must use GitHub Actions permissions and authentication appropriate for publishing packages to GHCR.

### Acceptance Criteria

A Docker image is pushed to GHCR when CI runs on the configured branches.

The pushed image can be identified by commit SHA.

The dev branch produces a stable dev image tag.

The workflow still runs Maven build validation before publishing the image.

### Out of Scope

Kubernetes deployment.

Kubernetes namespace creation.

Runtime application configuration changes.
features.name: Publish auth-service Docker image to GHCR

### Goal

Define the Kubernetes namespace and service account required to run auth-service.

### Context

auth-service needs Kubernetes deployment resources that are isolated in a dedicated namespace and can run under a dedicated service account.

### Scope

Add Kubernetes manifests for auth-service namespace and service account.

### Requirements

Kubernetes resources for auth-service must use a dedicated namespace.

auth-service must run using a dedicated Kubernetes service account.

The Kubernetes manifests must be suitable for automated deployment by GitHub Actions.

### Acceptance Criteria

A namespace manifest exists for auth-service.

A service account manifest exists for auth-service.

auth-service Kubernetes resources reference the intended namespace and service account.

The manifests can be validated with Kubernetes dry-run commands.

### Out of Scope

Deploying the application.

Creating real cluster secrets.

Changing the application source code.
features.name: Add Kubernetes namespace and service account

features.description:
### Goal

Enable Kubernetes to pull auth-service images from GHCR.

### Context

The auth-service Docker image will be published to GHCR. Kubernetes must be configured to authenticate when pulling the image, especially if the package is private.

### Scope

Update Kubernetes manifests and documentation to support GHCR image pull authentication.

### Requirements

auth-service Kubernetes configuration must support an image pull secret.

The service account must reference the image pull secret.

Documentation must explain how the image pull secret should be created for GHCR.

No real credentials or tokens may be committed.

### Acceptance Criteria

The service account references an image pull secret.

Documentation describes the required GHCR pull-secret setup.

No secret values are committed to the repository.

Kubernetes manifests remain valid for dry-run validation.

### Out of Scope

Creating real GitHub tokens.

Committing Kubernetes Secret credentials.

Changing the CI image publishing workflow.
features.name: Add GHCR image pull support for Kubernetes

features.description:
# Goal

Introduce an authentication API that integrates with Keycloak to support user registration and user authentication.

The service will act as the application's authentication gateway by exposing REST endpoints while delegating identity management and credential validation to Keycloak.

# Background

The Auth Service currently provides the application foundation, deployment pipeline, Kubernetes deployment, ingress, and runtime infrastructure.

The next capability is to expose authentication APIs backed by Keycloak so client applications can:

- register new users
- authenticate existing users
- receive authentication tokens issued by Keycloak

This feature establishes the initial integration between the Auth Service and the external identity provider.

# Scope

Implement an authentication module that includes:

- REST endpoints for user registration and login
- service layer responsible for communicating with Keycloak
- request/response DTOs required by the API
- Keycloak integration for:
  - creating users
  - authenticating users
  - obtaining access tokens
- configuration required for Keycloak connectivity
- dependency updates required for Keycloak integration

The implementation should follow the existing project architecture and dependency injection conventions.

# Architecture Notes

Introduce an Authentication capability composed of:

REST API

↓

Authentication Controller

↓

Authentication Services

↓

Keycloak Integration

↓

Keycloak Server

Responsibilities should remain clearly separated.

The controller should only expose the HTTP API.

Business logic should remain within the service layer.

Communication with Keycloak should be encapsulated inside dedicated integration services rather than spreading HTTP or Admin API calls throughout the application.

Configuration values should be externalized using the existing Spring Boot configuration mechanism.

The design should support future authentication features such as:

- refresh token
- logout
- password reset
- role management
- profile management

without requiring major architectural changes.

# Functional Requirements

Support user registration.

Support user login.

Authentication responses should return the token information produced by Keycloak.

User creation should be delegated to Keycloak.

Authentication should be delegated to Keycloak.

The Auth Service should not implement its own credential store.

# Configuration

Introduce any required application configuration for Keycloak connectivity, including values such as:

- Keycloak server URL
- realm
- client information
- authentication credentials

Configuration should remain environment-specific and compatible with the existing deployment model.

# Out of Scope

This ticket must not implement:

- authorization rules
- JWT validation filters
- refresh token endpoints
- logout endpoints
- role administration
- user profile management
- password recovery
- email verification
- social login
- MFA

These capabilities will be implemented in future tickets.

# Acceptance Criteria

- Registration endpoint is available.
- Login endpoint is available.
- Registration creates users in Keycloak.
- Login authenticates against Keycloak.
- Successful authentication returns the Keycloak-issued token payload.
- Required Keycloak configuration is externalized.
- Required project dependencies are added.
- The implementation follows the project's controller/service layering.
- Runtime validation demonstrates successful communication with a running Keycloak instance.

# Validation

Verify:

- project builds successfully
- application starts successfully
- registration creates a user in Keycloak
- login returns a valid token from Keycloak
- invalid credentials return an appropriate error
- configuration can be supplied through Spring Boot configuration without code changes

# Technical Notes

Prefer using the official Keycloak integration libraries where appropriate instead of implementing custom protocol logic when an official client is available.

Keep Keycloak-specific implementation details isolated behind service boundaries so future identity provider changes remain localized.

This feature should become the foundation for future authentication and authorization capabilities.
